page: Amazon Web Services i4i.12xlarge is an x86_64 storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is driven by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor providing 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with dedicated CPU allocation running at 3.5 GHz. It includes a 54 MB L3 cache, 384 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and 11,250 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The network interface supports a baseline throughput of 28 Gbps. Hardware acceleration features include AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions, while no discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark results show balanced general compute capabilities with a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,700 and a PassMark CPU score of 48,290.74, placing it within the middle 50% across standard synthetic benchmarks. Cryptographic throughput stands out, achieving a PassMark CPU encryption score of 43,100.5 (top 25%), assisted by hardware acceleration instructions. Memory subsystem tests register uncached read bandwidth of 161.73 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 70.12 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the instance delivers 44.86 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 39.68 GB/sec.

The inclusion of 11.25 TB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage provides dense local disk capacity without requiring dedicated network storage attachments, enhancing cost efficiency for high-IOPS operations. However, executing large language model generation shows clear resource limits on CPU hardware: while text generation on a 135M model reaches a strong 298.89 tokens per second, text generation on a 70B model falls to 2.76 tokens per second (bottom 25%). The instance is best suited for transactional and NoSQL databases, search engines, distributed storage nodes, and large-scale data processing that require heavy local IOPS paired with substantial RAM.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.12xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, paired with 384 GB of DDR4 RAM and 11,250 GB of local NVMe SSD storage on the Nitro hypervisor. It delivers 28 Gbps baseline network bandwidth alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid mid-tier multi-core computing (PassMark CPU score of 48,290.74) and top-tier encryption execution (43,100.5). Memory bandwidth reaches 161.73 GB/sec on uncached reads, supporting high throughput workloads such as Redis, which reached 44.86 million operations per second. While unsuited for large-scale LLM parameter generation without GPUs, its bundled NVMe storage and 8:1 memory-to-core ratio make it well suited for high-transaction databases, distributed caching, and search engine infrastructure.
